content: The dominant real-world OAuth account-linking bug class is trusting an unverified email claim: backends that link/create an account by the 'email' field in an OAuth/OIDC token without checking email_verified allow an attacker to pre-register with an email they don't own (or exploit domain-ownership changes) and later have a victim's 'Sign in with Google' silently merge into the attacker's existing account, handing over its data. Confused-deputy pattern (AWS cross-account, MCP proxy) generalizes as: never let an intermediary decide identity/scope on behalf of the caller using an ambient credential — bind every delegated action to an explicit, unguessable identifier scoped by the party being protected (AWS 'External ID' pattern; MCP RFC8707 resource-indicator / audience-bound tokens).
